title: Introduce credential fastpath and compact streaming shims across Python/TS/Go
author: Marisol Chen
description:
Motivation: Short-lived streaming sessions (single-chunk or very short chat turns) were dominated by auth/credential fetch latency and a handful of allocation-heavy path operations in each SDK. This PR adds a lightweight 'credential fastpath' API that reduces the median auth latency for short sessions and also introduces compact streaming shims to make generator/pullstream ergonomics consistent across Python, TypeScript, and Go.

Summary of changes: 1) credential fastpath: a non-blocking, cache-first credential fetch that returns a short-lived bearer when available and falls back to the existing credential resolution pipeline when not. The fastpath minimizes allocations and IO for common hot paths and is safe under concurrent refresh. 2) compact stream shims: small adapters that expose a uniform pull/generator surface for streaming responses in each SDK with a consistent .close/.cancel semantics and a minimal backpressure hint. 3) parity and version bumps: bring cross-SDK examples and typed signatures into alignment and bump package versions. 4) tests and benchmarks: new microbenchmarks for 1-4 chunk streaming sessions and an e2e integration for token refresh under streaming load.

Compatibility & safe rollout: The fastpath is opt-in via a new CredFastpathConfig and defaults to disabled for backward compatibility. When enabled it is feature-gated per-client. The streaming shim is additive and preserves existing streaming interfaces; we provide adapter helpers in each SDK so clients can migrate incrementally.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation in Python/TS/Go SDKs - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Microbenchmarks and docs updated - [x] Changelogs updated - [x] CI green

Context & motivation: ENG-1124 asked for a 15–25% latency reduction for short lived streams; the analysis showed auth path and stream iterator allocation churn were the dominant contributors. The approach taken here is conservative: add a fast, cache-first credential path and ergonomic adapters that reduce per-stream overhead without changing public semantics by default.

Notes for reviewers: pay particular attention to the concurrency model in the Go implementation (cred/fastpath.go) and the subtle race in the Python TTL refresh code (now fixed). See commit summaries for targeted diffs.
commit_summary: 3 commits: 1) add cred fastpath interfaces and core runtime (py/ts/go), 2) compact streaming adapters and examples, 3) tests/benchmarks/docs/changelog and version bumps
review_comments: Diego: Can we guard the fastpath with a runtime flag so infra teams can opt-out during rollout? -> Addressed: added CredFastpathConfig.enabled (default false).
Priya: TS tests flaked on CI due to timer mock; suggest using fake timers in bench harness. -> Addressed by switching to deterministic bench harness in fastpath.spec.ts.
Ethan: Go race detector reported a data race in the initial fastpath cache; fixed by switching to a mutex-protected double-checked init and added a unit test.
Author (Marisol): Added clarifying comments in code and a small section in docs about fallback semantics and recommended rollout strategy.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in 'credential fastpath' to reduce auth latency for short streaming sessions; add compact streaming shims for consistent generator/pullstream ergonomics across SDKs; bump SDK versions (python 3.2.0, typescript 1.6.0, go v1.9.0).
